# Surgery
## Overview
1. Scan the patient and identify the pathology. 2. Select the body region on the targeting doll. 3. Take the first tool in your active hand and apply it to the patient. 4. If the radial menu shows multiple procedures, choose the correct one. 5. Wait for the action to finish, then apply the next tool in the sequence. 6. After closing the access, perform a full rescan.
[color=#58e6d9]Cautery[/color] is an optional field-prep step in procedures where preparation is listed first. If you begin with Scalpel, that step is skipped. If you begin with Cautery, preparation is performed as the real first stage.
The operating table is not a hard requirement to start. The table, lighting, sterility, restraint, monitoring, ventilation, analgesia, sedation, and anesthesia all affect the deterministic result of the step. Insufficient conditions produce a compromised result: extra pain, contamination, bleeding, or a complication.
## Tools
The [color=#58e6d9]→[/color] arrow means the next tool. The opening Cautery can be skipped in sequences where Scalpel is listed immediately after it.
## Wounds and vessels
### 1. Deep wound treatment
Target: severe open wound, contamination, or necrosis.
Cautery → Scalpel → Hemostat → Retractor → Scalpel → MedicatedSuture.
### 2. Vessel repair
Target: vascular damage or an ongoing heavy blood source.
Cautery → Scalpel → Hemostat → Retractor → MedicatedSuture → Retractor → MedicatedSuture.
### 3. Wound irrigation
Target: contaminated or infected wound.
Cautery → Scalpel → Hemostat → Retractor → SyringeSaline → Retractor → MedicatedSuture.
### 4. Foreign body removal
Target: a wound with a separate foreign body.
Cautery → Scalpel → Hemostat → Retractor → Hemostat → Retractor → MedicatedSuture.
## Bones, tendons, and nerves
### 5. Fracture fixation
Target: confirmed fracture in the selected area.
Cautery → Scalpel → Hemostat → Retractor → Drill → Drill → Drill → MedicatedSuture.
### 6. Tendon repair
Target: tendon rupture or loss of integrity.
Cautery → Scalpel → Hemostat → Retractor → MedicatedSuture → Retractor → MedicatedSuture.
### 7. Peripheral nerve repair
Target: neurological deficit or nerve damage.
Cautery → Scalpel → Hemostat → Retractor → MedicatedSuture → Retractor → MedicatedSuture.
## Organs, brain, and eyes
### 8. Open internal organ access
Target: an internal organ in the selected area. This operation leaves the access open for later repair.
Cautery → Scalpel → Hemostat → Retractor → Scalpel → Retractor.
### 9. Repair open organ
Requirement: organ access is already open from operation #8.
Cautery → MedicatedSuture.
### 10. Skull decompression
Target: skull damage or an intracranial complication.
Cautery → Scalpel → Hemostat → Retractor → Drill → SyringeSaline → Retractor → MedicatedSuture.
### 11. Brain repair
Target: brain damage.
Cautery → Scalpel → Hemostat → Retractor → Scalpel → Retractor → MedicatedSuture → Retractor → MedicatedSuture.
### 12. Eye repair
Target: damaged eyes.
Cautery → Scalpel → Hemostat → Retractor → Scalpel → Retractor → MedicatedSuture → Retractor → MedicatedSuture.
### 13. Internal organ removal
Target: the selected internal organ.
Cautery → Scalpel → Hemostat → Retractor → Scalpel → Retractor → Saw → Retractor → MedicatedSuture.
### 14. Eye removal
Target: the eyes.
Cautery → Scalpel → Hemostat → Retractor → Scalpel → Retractor → Saw → Retractor → MedicatedSuture.
### 15. Internal organ transplantation
Requirement: the organ category is free; a compatible organ is in hand or nearby.
Cautery → Scalpel → Hemostat → Retractor → Scalpel → MedicatedSuture → Retractor → MedicatedSuture → MedicatedSuture.
### 16. Eye transplantation
Requirement: the eyes are removed; a compatible graft is in hand or nearby.
Cautery → Scalpel → Hemostat → Retractor → Scalpel → MedicatedSuture → Retractor → MedicatedSuture → MedicatedSuture.
## Limbs
### 17. Limb amputation
Target: the selected arm, hand, leg, or foot.
Cautery → Scalpel → Hemostat → Retractor → Saw → Retractor → MedicatedSuture.
### 18. Limb reattachment
Requirement: the limb category is free; a compatible detached part is in hand or nearby.
Cautery → Scalpel → Hemostat → Retractor → Scalpel → MedicatedSuture → Retractor → MedicatedSuture → MedicatedSuture.
## Forensics
### 19. Regional autopsy
Requirement: the patient is dead. Target: the selected body region.
Scalpel → Scalpel → Scalpel → MedicatedSuture.
## Cyberware
### 20. Internal cyberware installation
Requirement: a compatible physical module is in hand or nearby; the host organ slot is free.
Cautery → Scalpel → Hemostat → Retractor → Multitool → Retractor → MedicatedSuture.
### 21. Internal cyberware removal
Requirement: a compatible module is installed in the selected organ.
Cautery → Scalpel → Hemostat → Retractor → Multitool → Retractor → MedicatedSuture.
## Grafts
A graft is either a real detached body part or a factory-made mechanical replacement. The category must match a free category on the patient. After attachment, the part enters the living organ graph; a mechanical replacement automatically calibrates the neural interface.
